key_insight: CDSE improves self-evolving LLM agents by differentiating each skill into four coordinated functional components: Meta, Experience, Tool, and Script.
engineering_relevance: Role-specific skill updates and adaptive invocation offer a structured way to maintain reusable agent knowledge across planning, decisions, tool use, and execution.
method: Extract evidence-grounded semantic gradients from successful and failed trajectories.
Consolidate learning by functional role and apply component-specific updates and validation.
Coordinate components and adaptively invoke relevant skill knowledge.
evidence_signal: Across six benchmarks, three agent models, and two execution harnesses, CDSE led all 36 settings, averaging gains of 7.6 percentage points over Base and 2.6 points over the strongest competitor in each setting.
watch_item: Component-specific validation and cross-component coordination add implementation complexity; their operational overhead is not quantified in the abstract.
paper_title: From Trajectories to Differentiated Skills: Cognitive Differentiation for Self-Improving Agents
